questions.q: What actually gets deployed to the SSISDB catalog under the project deployment model?
options: An entire project — every package inside it, plus its parameters — built into a single .ispac file
Individual packages, one at a time, with no project-level grouping
Only the SSIS connection managers, not the packages themselves
A compiled .exe that runs independently of SQL Server
questions.explain: The project deployment model deploys a whole project — all its packages and parameters — as one .ispac unit, not package by package.

questions.q: Before you can Deploy Solution for an SSRS report project, which property must be set?
options: TargetServerURL, pointing at the destination Report Server
The report's RDL file must first be renamed to .rdlx
The Power BI workspace ID
The SQL Server Agent proxy account
questions.explain: TargetServerURL in the report project's properties tells Deploy Solution which Report Server to publish WorkOrderProductionSummary.rdl to.

questions.q: How does a finished Power BI report actually get into the Power BI Service?
options: Publish, from Power BI Desktop, choosing a destination workspace
Emailing the .pbix file to an administrator
Running a T-SQL script against the warehouse
It happens automatically the moment the .pbix file is saved
questions.explain: Power BI Desktop's Publish button pushes the .pbix's report and semantic model into a chosen workspace in the Power BI Service.

questions.q: What do the three deployment mechanics in this lesson — SSIS, SSRS, and Power BI — have in common?
options: Each builds a finished artifact locally, then pushes that artifact to a destination — the SSISDB catalog, a Report Server, or a Power BI Service workspace — rather than hand-editing anything on the destination itself
All three require the exact same deployment wizard
None of them can be automated or scripted
All three deploy directly to end users' desktops
questions.explain: Despite different mechanics, the pattern is the same: build once locally, then deploy the finished artifact — never hand-edit the destination.

questions.q: In this capstone's pipeline, which artifact deploys to the SSISDB catalog?
options: WorkOrderETL.dtsx's project, as an .ispac file
WorkOrderProductionSummary.rdl
The Power BI dashboard's .pbix file
The dw.FactWorkOrder table definition
questions.explain: WorkOrderETL.dtsx's project builds to an .ispac and deploys into SSISDB via the Integration Services Deployment Wizard.
